commits.message:
Read Word 98 for Mac files (nFib 0x00C2)

Word 98 for the Macintosh writes the Word 97 binary format with nFib
0x00C2. Its layout is identical to 0x00C1, but the parser refused these
files as 'older Word binary version'. All three such files in a local
corpus now convert; against Word's own .docx of each, paragraph counts
are equal, bold/italic/size/font/colour agree on every character, and
word similarity is 1.0, 0.999 and 1.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Name the real format of files that are not compound documents

A file named .doc that is RTF, PDF, a renamed .docx, a Word web page
(HTML/MHTML), Word 2003 XML, a Word for DOS/WordPerfect file, an Office
owner lock file (~$name.doc) or an empty/zero-filled download used to
fail with a bare 'Not a compound document'. sniffLegacyWordFile now
identifies it, and the parser throws LegacyWordNotCompoundException (a
FormatException with the same message prefix) carrying the kind so that
callers can route the file to the right reader or say what it is.

On a local corpus of 361 .doc files every one of the 15 non-compound
files is identified (2 RTF, 1 PDF, 10 lock files, 1 empty, 1 zero-filled).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Recover: omit contradictory comments or bookmarks instead of refusing

With recover, a comment table whose references miss their markers, or a
bookmark name table that contradicts its ranges (names over Word's 40
characters, duplicates, wrong counts), now costs only that feature. The
failed read is rolled back (stories, references, anchors and markers;
bookmarks and fields inside the comment story) and the omission is
declared: commentsOmitted (notesComments) or the new bookmarksOmitted
(fieldsLists). Without recover nothing changes.

Local corpus: the one document refused over comment markers now
converts (964k characters). The one refused over a bookmark name has
further damage (fields crossing stories, revision field boundaries) and
stays refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Recover the text of Word files whose compound directory is destroyed

Some .doc files have their FAT, directory and mini FAT sectors
overwritten (an interrupted save or copy). Word, LibreOffice and the
structured parser refuse them, but the WordDocument and table streams
are usually intact. recoverLegacyWordText finds the FIB, reads the
WordDocument stream (FAT chain when the FAT is still self-consistent,
else contiguously, bounded by cbMac) and locates the table stream as the
chain or contiguous run (any 64-byte boundary, for mini-stream tables)
whose bytes hold a piece table that validates at exactly fcClx and
accounts for every character. Text is then read through that piece
table exactly as extractLegacyWordText does.

convertLegacyWord(recover: true) falls back to a text-only DOCX when the
structured parse fails and the text is recoverable; the result has
recoveredTextOnly set and lists every limitation.

On 314 intact local .doc files the recovery path returns exactly the
same text as extractLegacyWordText in 312 (2 not recoverable, none
different). Of 11 damaged files, 5 are recovered; the other 6 have
fragmented or overwritten table streams and stay refused. With the
directory, FAT and mini FAT overwritten, 16 of 28 native fixtures are
recovered verbatim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
